title: Dynamic Sampling Orchestrator and Fidelity Proxy Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook documents the Dynamic Sampling Orchestrator (DSO) and Fidelity Proxy components used by the serving runtime to coordinate low-cost, high-signal profiling. It describes the architectural intent, sampling contracts, fidelity downgrade/upgrade semantics, operational runbook for experiments, benchmarks to validate signal quality, and the rollout/rollback checklist. This doc is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and applied ML engineers running fidelity experiments.

Motivation

- Profiling every request at full fidelity (full traces + KV captures + kernel timings) is too expensive at production scale.
- We need a way to: 1) sample requests adaptively to maximize root-cause signal, 2) ensure fidelity changes preserve SLOs, and 3) make sampling decisions auditable and reproducible for offline analysis.

Goals

1) Maintain production p95 latency SLO (default target: 95th <= 120ms for inference RPC) while collecting high-quality traces.
2) Allow experimenters to request arbitrary fidelity windows and get deterministic, reproducible sampling for evaluation workloads.
3) Provide a safe rollout path (canary -> cohort -> global) and automated safety checks (latency regressions, kernel slowdowns, cost delta).

Architecture (high level)

- Dynamic Sampling Orchestrator (service name: trace-orch): central policy engine; decides which requests to sample and at what fidelity.
- Fidelity Proxy (service name: fidelity-proxy): per-node agent that enforces sampling decisions and manages local buffering of high-fidelity payloads (KV snapshots, kernel timelines) to avoid backpressure on the request path.
- Telemetry Gateway (telemetry-gw): shuffles sampled payloads to the trace storage cluster (efficient path: ClickHouse for lightweight signals, Tempo for full traces, and S3 for archived kernel captures).
- Signal Bus (Kafka topic: profiling.signals): publish sampling decisions and metadata for downstream validation and audit.

Decision flow

1) Incoming request passes through request-classifier (runtime sidecar).
2) request-classifier sends a minimal decision-query to trace-orch (0.5ms p99 target).
3) trace-orch evaluates active policies and returns a sampling token with fidelity profile id (FPID).
4) fidelity-proxy receives token and applies local capture hooks. Large captures are stored to node-local disk and streamed to telemetry-gw asynchronously.

Sampling contracts and fidelity profiles

- Fidelity Profile (FPID): a small JSON manifest (versioned) describing captures and retention. Example fields: "trace_level": [light|standard|full], "kv_capture": [none|headers|prefix|full], "kernel_timings": [off|summary|full], "max_size_mb": n, "sample_weight": float.

- Contract guarantees:
  - If trace-orch returns an FPID, the fidelity-proxy will attempt to apply that profile; failures fall back to the next-fallback FPID(typically 'standard').
  - The orchestrator will not assign an FPID whose expected resource cost would exceed configured budget for the node or tenant.
  - FPID manifests are immutable after release; updates produce new FPIDs (semver).

- Default profiles we maintain:
  - low-signal: trace_level=light, kv_capture=none, kernel_timings=off, sample_weight=0.01
  - standard: trace_level=standard, kv_capture=headers, kernel_timings=summary, sample_weight=0.1
  - high-fidelity: trace_level=full, kv_capture=prefix, kernel_timings=full, sample_weight=1.0

Adaptive sampling algorithm (summary)

- Inputs: recent latency cohorts, kernel error rates, cold-start frequency, historical entropy of outputs.
- Outputs: an FPID assignment probability per request class.
- Key features:
  - Burst protection: stop increasing sampling during node-level thermal events.
  - Diversity heuristic: prioritize sampling across user cohorts to avoid measurement bias.
  - Reproducible seeding: sampling decisions derive from request_id + FPID salt so experiments can be replayed deterministically.

Fidelity Proxy internals

- Components: enforcer (applies FPID), capture buffer (capped circular buffer on local disk), uploader worker pool (streams to telemetry-gw), circuit-breaker (drop captures under pressure).
- Safety invariants:
  1) If disk usage > 65% of capture partition, circuit-breaker engages and downgrades to 'standard' for new captures.
  2) Uploader concurrency is rate-limited by node-configured egress bandwidth (default 25MB/s).
  3) Captures accepted for telemetry have an upper bound max_size_mb; oversized captures are truncated with metadata note.

Operational runbook: quick triage

1) Symptom: sudden increase in p95 latency correlated with deployment of a new FPID.
  - Step 1: Check trace-orch policy list: kubectl -n observability get cm fidelity-policies -o yaml
  - Step 2: Validate per-node circuit-breaker: kubectl logs fidelity-proxy-<node> | grep CIRCUIT_BREAKER
  - Step 3: Inspect sampling rate stream: kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --topic profiling.signals --from-beginning | jq .fpid | uniq -c
  - Step 4: If majority of nodes report circuit-breaker engagements, revert latest FPID roll (trace-orch rollback API).

2) Symptom: missing high-fidelity traces for a specific tenant cohort.
  - Step 1: Confirm active FPID for tenant: curl -s http://trace-orch.internal/api/v1/tenant/<tenant>/fpids
  - Step 2: Check fidelity-proxy accept logs for that tenant: journalctl -u fidelity-proxy | grep <tenant-id>
  - Step 3: Verify telemetry-gw ingress metrics (telemetry-gw/metrics HTTP). If telemetry-gw is saturated, enable graceful backpressure mode (telemetry-gw API /v1/backpressure/enable).

Benchmarks and validation

- Purpose: ensure sampled traces have sufficient signal and that sampling scheme does not materially change runtime SLOs.
- Minimum validation suite:
  1) Replay fidelity parity test: sample N=10k requests with both 'standard' and 'high-fidelity' FPIDs in shadow mode and compare kernel timing distributions (KS-statistic < 0.05 target).
  2) Latency impact test: measure p95 with profiling enabled vs disabled under 95th percentile traffic; acceptable delta <= 5% or 50ms whichever is smaller.
  3) Cost delta analysis: compute storage and egress delta per million requests; abort rollout if > 2x planned budget.

Benchmark harness commands (examples)

- Start a shadow sampling run:
  curl -X POST http://trace-orch.internal/api/v1/experiments \
    -d '{"name":"shadow-fidelity-parity-2026-09","target": "tenant:all","mode":"shadow","fpids":["standard","high-fidelity"],"duration_minutes":60}'

- Export sample manifests:
  kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --topic profiling.signals --timeout-ms 60000 | jq -r '
    "\(.request_id) \(.fpid) \(.timestamp)"' > /tmp/sampling-run.txt

Rollout and canary checklist

1) Pre-checks (automated):
  - All FPID unit tests pass.
  - Expected cost per 100k requests is under configured budget.
  - Shadow runs for 60 minutes show no p95 increase > 3%.
2) Canary (2% traffic, 4 nodes across zones):
  - Monitor: p95 latency, kernel_fails/sec, fidelity-proxy_truncations, telemetry-gw_ingress_errors.
  - Duration: min 2 hours at 99th percentile load.
3) Cohort rollout (20% traffic):
  - Run benchmark parity test on cohort traffic.
  - If any of the alerts fire (latency, cost, or disk pressure), immediately revert to previous FPID.
4) Global rollout: ramp to 100% over 6 hours with automated guardrails.

Automated safety checks (examples)

- Disk pressure alarm: node.capture_partition_free_bytes < 35% -> trigger fidelity-proxy downgrade
- Latency alarm: cohort_p95_delta > 7% AND absolute_delta > 60ms -> stop rollout
- Kernel error alarm: kernel_op_error_rate increased by factor > 3 -> hold rollout and notify kernel team

Operational APIs and quick commands

- Query current FPID for request class: curl http://trace-orch.internal/api/v1/query?class=chat-completion
- Start a canary: curl -X POST http://trace-orch.internal/api/v1/rollouts -d '{"fpid":"high-fidelity","traffic_pct":2}'
- Rollback last rollout: curl -X POST http://trace-orch.internal/api/v1/rollouts/rollback
- Inspect fidelity-proxy health: kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=fidelity-proxy -o wide; kubectl logs fidelity-proxy-<pod> -c enforcer

Data quality and postmortem guidance

- When an experiment fails, collect: sampling.signals Kafka segment, fidelity-proxy logs (one hour before/after), telemetry-gw metrics, ClickHouse sample index for the period.
- Run signal quality checks: verify coverage across user cohorts, check kernel timing correlation with trace-level events, and compute reproducibility rate (fraction of replayed requests that get same FPID).

Appendix: example FPID manifest (YAML)

---
fp_id: "fpid.high-fidelity.v1"
version: "1"
trace_level: full
kv_capture: prefix
kernel_timings: full
max_size_mb: 16
sample_weight: 1.0
retention_days: 7
---

Appendix: sample CLI for fidelity-proxy dry-run

# Enable dry-run mode (no uploads)
kubectl -n runtime exec -it fidelity-proxy-<pod> -- fidelity-proxyctl --mode=dry-run --fpids=standard,high-fidelity

# Check upload backlog
kubectl -n runtime exec fidelity-proxy-<pod> -- fidelity-proxyctl status | grep backlog

Ownership, metrics and SLOs

- Owner: eng-serving-runtime / Observability subteam (primary: @asha.patel).
- SLOs to watch when running profiling experiments:
  - Runtime p95 latency: target <= configured tenant SLO (default 120ms).
  - Telemetry ingress error rate: < 0.1%
  - Fidelity-proxy truncation rate for accepted captures: < 0.5%
  - Reproducibility (replay match rate): > 98% for deterministic experiments

Notes and open decisions

- Open: precise KS-statistic threshold for kernel timing parity is under review (current target 0.05).
- Open: centralized vs per-tenant sampling budgets — investigation ticket #ENG-9312.
